rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for an indicated or contrasted person, thing, or idea, especially one farther away than 呢.
Use 話 after a reporting verb or noun when the following clause gives what was said or reported.

example.english: I heard that he isn't going to work tomorrow.
example.traditional: 我聽人講話佢聽日唔返工。
example.jyutping: ngo5 teng1 jan4 gong2 waa6 keoi5 ting1 jat6 m4 faan1 gung1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for a person, thing, idea, or event already indicated or just mentioned.

example.english: I don't want that one; it's too expensive.
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 soeng2 jiu3 go2 go3 taai3 gwai3 laa3

rows.note: Use this colloquial result construction when the first part is so extreme that it produces the following result.

example.english: I was so tired that I couldn't walk.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gui6 dou3 haang4 m4 juk1

rows.note: Use this relative-clause construction when English uses “that” to link a clause to the noun it describes.

example.english: This is the book that I bought yesterday.
example.jyutping: ni1 bun2 hai6 ngo5 cam4 jat6 maai5 ge3 syu1

rows.note: Use this when a clause modifies a reporting noun, as in the rumour that they got married.

example.english: I heard the rumour that they got married.
example.traditional: 我聽到佢哋結婚嘅傳聞。
example.jyutping: ngo5 teng1 dou2 keoi5 dei6 git3 fan1 ge3 cyun4 man4

rows.note: Use this for the place slice of relative “that,” meaning “where” or “to which.”

example.english: This is the place that we ate at last time.
example.traditional: 呢間就係我哋上次食飯嗰度。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 zau6 hai6 ngo5 dei6 soeng6 ci3 sik6 faan6 go2 dou6

rows.note: Use this for the time slice of relative “that,” meaning “when.”

example.english: Do you remember that time when we first met?
example.traditional: 你記唔記得我哋第一次見面嗰陣？
example.jyutping: nei5 gei3 m4 gei3 dak1 ngo5 dei6 dai6 jat1 ci3 gin3 min6 go2 zan6
